subject: BrightPath Dedicated: Tiered compute allocation proposal
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: BrightPath Dedicated: Tiered compute allocation proposal

Team — attaching a concise recommendation for BrightPath's Dedicated commitment. High level: they want predictable latency for multi-turn retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) plus a low-cost path for high-volume event-type inference. After modeling their query profile (attached spreadsheet) I recommend a three-tier pool with clear slotting and fallback rules.

TL;DR: propose an initial reserved pool split 40% H100 / 35% A100 / 25% L4 with the following rationale: 
- H100 (40%): primary for memory-heavy large-context models (16k+ context, heavy kv cache) and for models that need FP16/TF32 performance for low-latency scoring.
- A100 (35%): throughput-optimized for mid-context lengths (~2k–8k), best cost/perf for batch scoring and many concurrent short chat sessions.
- L4 (25%): serve as cost-efficient scale for quantized 4-bit models (int4/int8 dequantization pipelines) for high QPS, short-context transforms, and trickle/async tasks.

Key operational controls and tradeoffs considered:
- Memory headroom: H100 nodes should be provisioned with >=20% headroom for KV cache growth and model-peek bursts. For models requiring >80GB effective working memory we should place them on H100 with model-sharding rather than attempt spill-to-disk on A100.
- Token latency vs tokens/$: A100 offers the best tokens-per-dollar on batch workloads; L4 wins for short single-turn ops when models are aggressively quantized and pruning is acceptable.
- Fallbacks: requests hitting memory limits will automatically route to an H100-compatible variant (smaller replica or quantized variant) with degraded but safe QoS. Routing policy: latency-sensitive routes prefer H100 then A100; cost-sensitive routes prefer L4 then A100.
- Autoscale & burst: reserved baseline with reserved slots mapped to each tier + burst pool in Hosted capacity for unexpected spikes. Burst debit accounting in the spreadsheet (tab: economics).

Operational notes for engineering/ops:
- Kernel selection: prefer optimized fused-attention kernels on H100 and A100; avoid kernel fallbacks that degrade throughput for long-context H100 runs.
- Quantization: validate accuracy regressions for L4 with the customer's eval set (see mutual_action_plan.docx). If accuracy drop >6% on key prompts, reduce L4 baseline and reassign to A100.
- Cache strategy: prefix/KV caching for multi-turn sessions should be colocated to avoid cross-host KV fetches; recommend sticky session routing for first 3 turns.

Costs (modeling summary, see xlsx): estimated monthly spend for BrightPath pilot (baseline QPS 180k/month) 
- H100 reserved (40%): $42k/mo equivalent 
- A100 reserved (35%): $28k/mo equivalent 
- L4 reserved (25%): $8k/mo equivalent 
Projected blended tokens/$ improves by ~18% vs all-H100 baseline.

Ask: please review and call out any operational concerns. Need Vivek to sign off on the fallback/autoscale configuration and Jasmine to confirm the mutual action plan items before I share the deck with BrightPath's CTO.

Attachments: brightpath_sku_modeling.xlsx, brightpath_compute_strategy.pdf, mutual_action_plan.docx

Thanks,
Irene
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: BrightPath Dedicated: Tiered compute allocation proposal

Irene — solid work, this reflects their profile well. A couple quick operational questions:

1) Burst accounting: how aggressive is the burst lending from Hosted? Do we have a hard cap on burst percent per customer to avoid noisy neighbor risk? Recommend a default 25% of reserved capacity as burstable to Hosted, gated by QoS and circuit-breaker.

2) L4 baseline: your proposed 25% seems low if they plan to offload a large fraction of ephemeral classification calls. Can we model a scenario with 40% L4 / 30% H100 / 30% A100 and show accuracy/cost delta? If accuracy holds on eval set, that might be a more saleable number.

Otherwise I'm comfortable with the failover routing and sticky-session idea. If we increase L4 baseline we'll need a stricter rollout plan for quantized models (canary on 5% traffic, measure top-1/top-3 distributions, rollback at 3 sigma).

—Vivek
Head of Product Ops
